ITEM TRANSCRIPT
Food
safety
largely
hinges
on
proper
cleaning
,
and
it's
important
to
know
that
not
all
foods
are
cleaned
the
same
way
.
Some
foods
,
like
leafy
greens
,
berries
,
and
raw
meats
,
should
be
kept
clean
.
These
items
often
come
into
contact
with
dirt
,
pesticides
,
or
bacteria
during
cultivation
or
processing
,
so
a
thorough
rinse
is
necessary
.
On
the
other
hand
,
some
foods
,
such
as
root
vegetables
like
potatoes
and
beets
,
can
only
have
their
outside
parts
washed
with
cold
water
.
Their
skins
act
as
a
natural
barrier
,
and
washing
the
exterior
with
a
brush
is
enough
to
remove
surface
grime
.
Then
there's
pre
washed
produce
.
Many
supermarkets
sell
items
like
bagged
salads
and
pre
cut
melons
that
have
already
been
cleaned
.
These
are
labeled
as
safe
to
eat
without
additional
washing
,
so
there's
no
need
to
rinse
them
again
.
For
fruits
and
vegetables
with
peels
,
such
as
bananas
,
oranges
,
and
cucumbers
,
use
cold
water
to
wash
the
outside
.
Cold
water
helps
prevent
the
loss
of
nutrients
and
keeps
the
produce
fresh
.
If
you
buy
packaged
food
,
always
read
the
label
carefully
.
It
will
clearly
indicate
whether
the
product
needs
washing
.
If
it's
prewashed
or
marked
ready
to
eat
,
doing
nothing
is
the
best
course
of
action
to
avoid
introducing
new
contaminants
.
